henry.title: Loch Ness Layers: Why the Deep Water Stays Cold
henry.intro: Make a tiny loch in a glass. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: 🧰 Get a glass, cold water, warm water, 2 food colors.
🔵 Fill the glass with cold blue water.
🔴 Pour warm red water onto a spoon, slowly.
👀 Look from the side. Draw what you see.

handsOn.title: 🧪 Build a mini loch
steps: 1. Cold blue water in the glass. Warm red water in the cup.
2. Hold the spoon above the blue. Pour red onto the spoon. Go slow!
3. Look from the side. Red sits on top. Cold water is denser.
4. Stir to mix. Purple means mixed.
handsOn.look: Where is the line between red and blue? That line is like the layers in a real loch.
handsOn.q: Which layer was on top, warm or cold?

worksheet: Guess first: will the warm red water go on TOP or SINK? Circle one.
The warm red water stayed on: TOP / BOTTOM (circle)
Draw your glass. Color the red layer and the blue layer.
Cold water is denser. In Loch Ness, cold water stays at the: TOP / BOTTOM
Challenge: after stirring, my water turned ____________.

passage.text: 🏞️ A loch is a Scottish lake. Loch Ness is about 230 m deep. That is very deep!
❄️ Deep in Loch Ness the water stays cold, about 5°C. Cold water is denser. That means heavier for its size, so it sinks.
passage.q: Which water sinks, cold or warm?

passage.text: 🌬️ Wind can stir a loch. Stirring mixes warm and cold water together.

words: one level on top of another
henry.challenge: 🥄 Stir your glass with the spoon. What color does it turn? Why?

frankie.title: Rain Cloud in a Jar ☁️🌧️
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: Scotland has lots of rain! Let's make a rain cloud in a jar. (About 13 minutes.)
steps: ☁️ Spray a foam cloud on the water.

handsOn.title: ☁️ Make rain
handsOn.look: Grown-up: the cloud holds water until it gets too heavy, just like a real cloud.

worksheet: Draw your cloud and the rain falling.

Scotland is rainy. Circle the weather:
☔ ☀️ 🌵

Count the raindrops and circle the number:
💧💧💧💧   3   4   5
Color the cloud grey and the rain blue ☁️

Stretch: Trace R, then write your own R:
RRR ______
